---
title: "Speech Intelligibility in Parkinson’s Disease"
subtitle: "A Research Study at the University of Houston"
---

## About the Study

Many people living with Parkinson’s disease notice changes in their speech over time. These changes can make it more difficult for others to understand them in everyday conversations.

Speech-language pathologists work to evaluate and treat these changes, but measuring how understandable someone’s speech is—called *speech intelligibility*—is not always straightforward. Clinicians often rely on quick judgments, and these can vary from one clinician to another.

This study is designed to better understand speech in Parkinson’s disease and to improve how clinicians evaluate speech clarity. To do this, we are collecting speech recordings from individuals with Parkinson’s disease that will help us build better tools for assessment and treatment.

## What participation involves

Participation includes a single visit to the University of Houston.

During your visit, you will:

-   Provide some background information about your health and communication
-   Complete brief hearing and cognitive screenings
-   Participate in speaking tasks, including:
-   Reading short passages and sentences
-   Engaging in simple speaking activities (e.g., conversation)

Your speech will be audio recorded during these tasks.

The session will take approximately 60–90 minutes, and you may take breaks at any time.

## Who can participate

You may be eligible if you:

-   Have been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease
-   Speak English
-   Do not have other neurological conditions (e.g., stroke, traumatic brain injury)

## Compensation

Participants will receive a \$50 gift card after completing the session.
